blockers: Union must maintain internal credibility on staffing improvements.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: A strong vote does not contradict settlement if it is used as bargaining leverage rather than trigger for immediate walkout.
endpoint_ledger.description: Parties reach a tentative agreement or formal standstill that averts a walkout while leaving implementation details for later.
endpoint_ledger.label: Pre-strike settlement or standstill

meta.important_question: Will the parties reach a meaningful settlement or standstill agreement before any actual walkout begins?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Scenario explicitly includes settlement as a plausible branch and city mediation as a mechanism.
realization_criteria: A signed tentative agreement, memorandum of understanding, or publicly confirmed standstill is announced by bargaining parties.
No strike start time is executed before the agreement or standstill takes effect.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Authorization vote creates leverage but no terminal choice has yet been made; mediation channel remains open.

blockers: Cautious and reluctant nurse cohorts may not cross mobilization threshold.
Public backlash risk could deter leadership.
Mediation or concessions could delay action.
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: A high authorization vote alone does not realize this endpoint without actual work stoppage execution.
endpoint_ledger.description: Union proceeds from authorization to an observable strike or comparable work stoppage affecting hospital operations.

meta.important_question: Will the authorization vote translate into a real strike or comparable work stoppage?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Scenario names strike as a core endpoint option and highlights mobilization threshold dynamics.
realization_criteria: Union announces and executes a strike start date or equivalent work stoppage.
Hospital operations are altered by nonattendance, picketing, or formal strike designation.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Strike is threatened but not yet scheduled; support appears meaningful but not unanimous.

blockers: Legal standards may be unfavorable or unclear.
Aggressive legal action may worsen public legitimacy.
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Exploring contingency staffing does not itself imply a legal filing.
endpoint_ledger.description: Hospital leadership pursues injunction or comparable legal mechanism to limit or delay strike action.
endpoint_ledger.label: Management seeks legal restraint

meta.important_question: Will hospital leadership attempt an injunction or similar legal restraint rather than relying only on bargaining and contingency staffing?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Decision authority likely sits with executives subject to board risk tolerance, making this a distinct terminal option.
realization_criteria: Hospital files for injunction, emergency order, or similar legal restraint related to labor action.
Executives publicly or formally rely on legal intervention as a principal dispute pathway.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Scenario includes injunction attempt as plausible but provides no evidence it has started at T0.

blockers: Strong patient-safety evidence may protect union legitimacy.
Management may absorb blame if understaffing appears avoidable.
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Sympathy for nurses can coexist with short-term frustration until narrative clearly consolidates.
endpoint_ledger.description: If care disruptions occur, the dominant public narrative assigns main responsibility to the union's escalation choices.
endpoint_ledger.label: Public backlash primarily targets union

meta.important_question: If procedures are canceled or delayed, does public blame fall mainly on management or on the union?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Scenario explicitly names public backlash as a branch and families as a swing audience.
realization_criteria: Sustained media, family, or civic statements predominantly blame union action for cancellations or patient harm.
Observable public pressure causes union approval or coalition support to materially decline.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Backlash is possible but not dominant at T0 because families are mixed and disruption is prospective.

blockers: Visible patient cancellations may be easier to attribute to strike threat than chronic understaffing.
Management budget frame may persuade some audiences.
Public attention may decay without salient incidents.
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Management can still reach settlement even if blame rises; blame assignment is not identical to bargaining outcome.
endpoint_ledger.description: If care disruptions or safety concerns intensify, the dominant narrative assigns main responsibility to executive decisions and understaffing.
endpoint_ledger.label: Public backlash primarily targets management

meta.important_question: If procedures are canceled or delayed, does public blame fall mainly on management or on the union?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Scenario's causal premise gives management ownership exposure through staffing deterioration and budget defense.
realization_criteria: Sustained media, family, or civic statements predominantly blame executive staffing and bargaining choices.
Observable public pressure pushes management into concessions, reputational retreat, or board intervention.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Worsening staffing ratios create a credible blame pathway against management before any walkout occurs.

simulation_brief.scale: single fictional urban hospital and surrounding civic environment
simulation_brief.source_summary: Fictional hospital nurses' union announces a strike authorization vote after staffing ratios worsen. Hospital executives cite budget constraints. Patients' families fear canceled procedures. City officials can mediate but cannot impose a contract. Traveling nurse agencies may benefit.
simulation_brief.time_zero_posture: pre-strike escalation with unresolved bargaining pressure
simulation_brief.title: hospital_nurses_union_staffing_dispute
uncertainty_notes: No city size, hospital size, or bargaining unit size specified.
No explicit legal jurisdiction for health-care strike rules or injunction standards.
No explicit current contract status or exact staffing ratio data.

sociology_baseline.evidence: Actors are more persuadable by frames near existing values such as patient safety or care continuity.
Actual strike participation likely depends on perceived supermajority support after authorization vote.
Fear of isolation and dependency discourage open dissent or support.
Nurses are influenced by coworker networks; families by similar care situations and local information channels.
Escalation support becomes more likely when multiple trusted peers signal readiness.
Professional identity, labor solidarity, and management role boundaries structure interpretation.
Absent fresh disruption or dramatic bargaining news, public attention may fade quickly.

sociology_prompt_influences.description: Claims tied to unsafe staffing are more resonant than abstract compensation rhetoric.
Threats to procedures and continuity rapidly increase family attention and backlash potential.
Management justification has some credibility with elites but weaker resonance if service quality appears to decline.
Nonbinding mediation can help both sides justify temporary de-escalation without surrender.
